\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{полицейский} (politséyskiy)}{полицейский (politséyskiy)}]{\ru{полицейский} (politséyskiy) — a police officer}

\label{lesson:RU-C108-police-officer}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for a nurse, then the Russian for a cook.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{полицейский}}
\textbf{\ru{полицейский}} (\emph{politséyskiy}) — \textquotedblleft{}a police officer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{полицейский}} is an adjective from \emph{\ru{полиция}}, \textquotedblleft{}police\textquotedblright{}, standing alone: \textquotedblleft{}a police officer\textquotedblright{}. \emph{\ru{полиция}} came, from Peter the Great's time, through Polish \emph{policja} or German \emph{Polizei} from Latin \emph{polītīa}, Greek \emph{politeía}, \textquotedblleft{}citizenship, government\textquotedblright{} (Vasmer).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{politséyskiy}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{politséyskiy}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{politséyskiy}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Russian for a nurse, then the Russian for a cook, then say \emph{politséyskiy} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{продавец} (prodavéts)}{продавец (prodavéts)}]{\ru{продавец} (prodavéts) — a shop assistant}

\label{lesson:RU-C108-shop-assistant}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for a cook, then the Russian for a police officer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{продавец}}
\textbf{\ru{продавец}} (\emph{prodavéts}) — \textquotedblleft{}a shop assistant\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{продавец}} is \emph{\ru{продавать}}, \textquotedblleft{}to sell\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{-\ru{ец}}, \textquotedblleft{}one who does it\textquotedblright{}. The verb is \emph{\ru{про}-} with \emph{\ru{давать}}, \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{}. Vasmer takes \emph{\ru{давать}} from \emph{\ru{дать}}, \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{}, kin to Lithuanian \emph{dovanà}, \textquotedblleft{}a gift\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}
